description: An oncology department administrator must finalize whether and how to operate a proposed Saturday infusion clinic for two patients, including the patient served, chair capacity, start time, medication preparation, and the alternate arrangement for the other patient, with input from infusion nursing, pharmacy, facilities, and patient navigation.

shared_context.S1: The oncology department has proposed a Saturday infusion clinic for two patients, Patient A and Patient B, who both need treatment arrangements for this weekend.
shared_context.S2: Morgan makes the binding decision about the Saturday clinic operating plan.
shared_context.S3: The clinic area normally has two infusion chairs and uses the department's standard Saturday opening workflow.
shared_context.S4: The department's routine pre-opening huddle includes infusion nursing, pharmacy, facilities, and patient navigation before the administrator finalizes the plan.

PF1.text: Patient A's order requires two hours of post-infusion observation, and the only Saturday RN credentialed for that observation protocol is available from 08:00 to 12:00; no RN with that credential is available later that day.

PF2.text: Patient A's medication must be compounded in the oncology cleanroom and released to the clinic by 07:30 Saturday for an 08:00 administration; it cannot be prepared safely at chairside after the clinic opens.

PF3.text: Infusion chair 2 failed its electrical safety inspection Friday and is tagged out until Monday, leaving only chair 1 available Saturday.

PF4.text: Patient B already has a confirmed appointment at the partner infusion center for Monday at 09:00, and the patient has accepted that appointment as the alternate treatment arrangement.

acceptance_conditions: The Saturday clinic must open for Patient A.
The plan must use exactly one infusion chair.
Pharmacy must commit to compounding and releasing Patient A's medication by 07:30 Saturday.
Patient B's alternate treatment must be confirmed for Monday at 09:00 at the partner infusion center.
The RN credential and availability fact must be cited as justification for serving Patient A at 08:00.

content_checks.C5: any(c['target'] == 'Ravi' and 'Patient A' in c['detail'] and '07:30' in c['detail'] and ('release' in c['detail'] or 'released' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['target'] == 'Noah' and 'Patient B' in c['detail'] and 'Monday' in c['detail'] and '09:00' in c['detail'] and 'partner infusion center' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed
provenance_checks.P4: 'PF4' in credited_facts and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The qualified RN's 08:00-12:00 availability and Patient A's two-hour observation requirement change the selected patient to Patient A and the clinic start time to exactly 08:00.
The cleanroom requirement and 07:30 release deadline change the pharmacy plan from unspecified preparation to a commitment to release Patient A's medication by exactly 07:30 Saturday.
The failed inspection changes the operating capacity from the normal two chairs to exactly one available chair.
The accepted booking changes Patient B's alternate arrangement from unspecified follow-up to the partner infusion center appointment on Monday at exactly 09:00.
